scenarios.title: Coffee Before Work
scenarios.role: a barista at a busy city-centre café
scenarios.setting: The counter of a café at 8:30 on a weekday morning. The learner is ordering breakfast before work and the queue is short but moving.
scenarios.goal: Order a coffee and something to eat, ask about a milk alternative, and confirm the total price before paying.
usefulLanguage: Could I get a medium latte, please?
Do you have oat milk?
What's in the breakfast wrap?
Can I have that to take away?
How much is that altogether?
Sorry, could you say that again?
That's everything, thanks.
scenarios.opening: Morning! What can I get for you today?

scenarios.title: Hotel Check-in
scenarios.role: a receptionist at a small city hotel
scenarios.setting: The hotel lobby at three in the afternoon. The learner has a booking for two nights and is tired after a long journey.
scenarios.goal: Check in, confirm how many nights are booked, and ask about breakfast times and the wifi password.
usefulLanguage: I have a reservation under the name Chen.
Is breakfast included in the price?
What time does breakfast finish?
Could I have the wifi password, please?
Is it possible to have a room away from the street?
Sorry, I didn't catch that.
Thank you, that's very helpful.
scenarios.opening: Good afternoon, welcome to the Parkview Hotel. Do you have a reservation with us?

scenarios.title: Job Interview
scenarios.role: a hiring manager at a small marketing agency
scenarios.setting: A video interview for a junior marketing role. The learner has two years of experience and the interview is in its first ten minutes.
scenarios.goal: Present your relevant experience clearly, explain why you want this particular company, and ask one thoughtful question about the role.
usefulLanguage: I've spent the last two years working on social media campaigns.
What attracted me to your agency was its work with local brands.
In my current role, I'm responsible for planning and reporting.
One example that comes to mind is a campaign we ran last spring.
I'd say my main strength is staying calm under pressure.
Could you tell me more about how the team is structured?
That's a good question — let me think for a moment.
scenarios.opening: Thanks for joining us today. To start, could you tell me a little about yourself?

scenarios.title: Missed Connection
scenarios.role: an airline service desk agent at a large airport
scenarios.setting: The airline service desk at nine in the evening. The learner's first flight was delayed and the connecting flight has already left.
scenarios.goal: Explain what happened, ask to be rebooked on the next available flight, confirm what happens to your checked bag, and request a meal voucher.
usefulLanguage: My first flight was delayed, so I missed my connection.
Could you put me on the next flight to Manchester?
Will my suitcase be sent on with me?
Is there anything earlier tomorrow morning?
Do I need to collect my bag and check in again?
Would it be possible to get a meal voucher?
What time should I be back at the gate?
scenarios.opening: Good evening. How can I help you at the service desk?

scenarios.title: At the Doctor's
scenarios.role: a general practitioner at a local clinic
scenarios.setting: A ten-minute appointment at a walk-in clinic. The learner has had a sore throat and a cough for four days.
scenarios.goal: Describe your symptoms and how long you have had them, ask whether you need medicine, and find out if you should stay off work.
usefulLanguage: I've had a sore throat since Monday.
It hurts when I swallow.
I've also been coughing a lot at night.
Do I need to take anything for it?
Should I stay at home from work?
How long will it take to get better?
Is it okay to drink coffee with this?
scenarios.opening: Come in, take a seat. What seems to be the problem?

scenarios.title: Flat Viewing
scenarios.role: a letting agent showing a one-bedroom flat
scenarios.setting: A viewing of a furnished one-bedroom flat on the second floor. The learner is looking for somewhere to live for at least a year.
scenarios.goal: Ask about the rent and bills, the deposit, and the length of the contract, then arrange a second viewing before deciding.
usefulLanguage: Does the rent include water and heating?
How much deposit would I need to pay?
How long is the minimum contract?
Is the furniture included in the price?
How far is the nearest supermarket?
Would it be possible to see the flat again on Saturday?
I'd like a day or two to think it over.
scenarios.opening: Hi, thanks for coming. So this is the one-bedroom on the second floor — what would you like to know first?

scenarios.title: Office Hours
scenarios.role: a lecturer in economics holding weekly office hours
scenarios.setting: The lecturer's office on a Wednesday afternoon. The learner is worried about the upcoming essay and missed two seminars because of illness.
scenarios.goal: Explain the difficulty you are having, ask about the extension policy, and agree a clear plan with the lecturer for finishing the essay.
usefulLanguage: I'm struggling with the second part of the essay question.
I missed two seminars because I was ill.
Could you clarify what you mean by 'critical evaluation'?
What's the procedure if I need an extension?
Would it be acceptable to focus on one case study?
So, to confirm, the new deadline would be the fifteenth?
Thank you — that makes things much clearer.
scenarios.opening: Hello — come in. You wanted to talk about the assignment, is that right?

scenarios.title: Internet Down
scenarios.role: a call-centre agent for a home internet provider
scenarios.setting: A phone call to customer support. The learner's home internet has been down for two days and they work from home.
scenarios.goal: Explain the problem, answer the security questions, book a technician visit, and note down the reference number and appointment time.
usefulLanguage: My internet has been down since Tuesday morning.
I've already restarted the router twice.
The light on the box is flashing red.
Could you send an engineer this week?
I'm available on Thursday afternoon.
Sorry, could you repeat the reference number?
What should I do if it's still not working after the visit?
scenarios.opening: Good morning, you're through to CityNet support. My name is Alex. How can I help?

scenarios.title: Complaint at Dinner
scenarios.role: the manager of a mid-range Italian restaurant
scenarios.setting: A restaurant table at eight in the evening. The learner's main course arrived cold after a forty-minute wait, and a side dish was missing.
scenarios.goal: Complain politely but firmly, ask for the dish to be replaced, and discuss having the item removed from the bill without ruining the evening.
usefulLanguage: I'm afraid this dish has gone cold.
We ordered the salad as well, but it never arrived.
We've been waiting quite a long time.
Could you bring us a fresh one, please?
I'd rather not pay for a dish I couldn't eat.
I don't want to make a fuss, but it's disappointing.
Would you be able to take it off the bill?
scenarios.opening: Good evening — I'm the manager here. I understand there was a problem with your meal?

scenarios.title: Conference Reception
scenarios.role: the founder of a small design studio at an industry conference
scenarios.setting: The evening reception of a design conference. People are standing in small groups with drinks, and the learner has come alone.
scenarios.goal: Introduce yourself, explain your work in a way that invites conversation, find shared interests, and suggest staying in touch without being pushy.
usefulLanguage: I don't think we've met — I'm Lin, from Hangzhou.
I work on the product side, mostly with early-stage teams.
What brought you to the conference this year?
That's interesting — we've run into something similar.
It sounds like we're both trying to solve the same problem.
Would you be open to a quick call next week?
Let me send you my details rather than take up your evening.
scenarios.opening: Hi there — quite a turnout tonight. Is this your first time at the conference?

scenarios.title: Finding the Museum
scenarios.role: a shopkeeper standing outside a corner shop
scenarios.setting: A street corner in an unfamiliar part of town. The learner wants to reach the city museum and has no map on their phone.
scenarios.goal: Ask for directions, follow the landmarks described, confirm how long the walk takes, and repeat the route back to check you understood.
usefulLanguage: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the museum?
Is it far from here?
So I go straight, then turn left at the bank?
How long does it take on foot?
Is there a bus that goes there?
Let me make sure I've got that right.
Thanks a lot — you've been very helpful.
scenarios.opening: Hello — you look a bit lost. Can I help you find something?

scenarios.title: Negotiating a Deadline
scenarios.role: the project lead at a client company
scenarios.setting: A video call two days before a report is due. The learner's team has hit unexpected delays and needs more time without losing the client's trust.
scenarios.goal: Explain the delay honestly, propose a specific one-week extension with a revised plan, and agree on an interim update so the client stays confident.
usefulLanguage: I wanted to flag a scheduling risk before it becomes a problem.
The delay is mainly down to a change in the data we received.
Would it be realistic to agree on Friday the twenty-sixth instead?
In the meantime, I can send you a progress summary on Wednesday.
I appreciate the deadline is important on your side too.
What would make this work for you?
Let me confirm that in writing after the call.
scenarios.opening: Thanks for making time. I saw your email about the deadline — what's the situation?
